title: ask-lattice-quickscan-and-implementation-hunches-2026-08
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable synthesis of recent field conversations (Aug 2026), surface lightweight implementation hunches for engineering/product to triage. This is not a final roadmap — it’s a prioritized note-to-eng for fast probes and low-friction wins.

Context / how this doc was made:
- Collated 18 customer interviews (topline notes), 42 support threads, and two postmortems from high-latency incidents.
- Emphasis on asks that appear in multiple accounts AND where we have a plausible small-scope change that could materially improve experience or reduce support churn.
- Customers sampled: mid-market SaaS (analytics), two AI-native startups, one payment platform, one regulated healthcare org.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Customers cluster around three pain areas: predictable latency for short-chat use cases, cost-transparent guidance for serving configuration, and migration friction when moving from prototype to Dedicated or Private. Top immediate probes: (1) lightweight per-route latency SLA indicators in Console, (2) a cost-suggestion assistant for common workload patterns, (3) a small SDK helper to persist and rehydrate KV/cache prefixes to reduce cold-start tail latency. Each probe can be scoped as a 1–3 sprint spike + quick follow-up experiment.

Top 6 asks (annotated vignettes + impact):
1) "Give me an early signal if my route is going to violate latency SLOs" — Customer vignette: analytics product schedules synchronous summarization on user actions; occasional 700–900ms spikes cause front-end timeouts.
   - Frequency: high (mentioned by 6 customers)
   - Business impact: high (lost UX, support load)
   - Implementation hunch: add per-route 95/99th rolling latency indicator in Console; surface a red/yellow/green badge and link to recent traces. Backend: aggregate existing metrics (per-route p95/p99) and expose via Console widgets. UI work + metric rollup.
   - Rough effort: 2 frontend sprints + 1 infra sprint to materialize aggregated metric views.

2) "How do we size for Dedicated without overcommitting?" — Enterprise buyer asks for deterministic guidance: given throughput targets, what GPU class and commit tier?
   - Frequency: medium (RFPs + two deal conversations)
   - Business impact: high (sales conversion)
   - Implementation hunch: generate a simple Dedicated Sizing Wizard in Console: user inputs target qps, median prompt length, concurrency. We already have perf profiles per-model — reuse that to produce a recommended pool config and expected cost/latency curves.
   - Rough effort: 1 product, 1 data engineer, 1 SRE spike (2–3 weeks)

3) "Make prefix cache explicit and easy to reuse" — Startups using streaming chat report cold-start immaturity when sessions rehydrate; developer time is spent wiring in custom KV persistence.
   - Frequency: medium-high (observed in 4 startups)
   - Impact: medium (latency reduction for chat apps; developer productivity)
   - Implementation hunch: ship a small SDK helper method + docs: persist_prefix(session_id, bucket) and rehydrate_prefix(session_id). On server side, enable a first-class API for saving/restoring KV cache blobs (encrypted) with TTL.
   - Rough effort: 2 sprints across SDK + runtime API (low infra risk).

4) "Explain cost implications of batching and quantization" — Customers want quick readouts: what happens to latency/cost/quality if I apply 4-bit quantization or increase batch size from 1->8?
   - Frequency: high among PLG users
   - Impact: high on billing transparency and product trust
   - Implementation hunch: cost-sim report in Console that simulates token-level cost for a sample workload. Use historic token distribution + our kernel perf profiles to estimate latency and cost ranges. Present easy toggles for quantization and batch size.
   - Rough effort: 2–3 sprints (data + UI + small modeling work).

5) "Rollout fallback behavior when a model variant is unavailable" — Cases where hosted capacity bump leads to degraded completions; customers want predictable automatic fallback rules per route.
   - Frequency: medium (support escalations)
   - Impact: medium-high (reliability perception)
   - Implementation hunch: expose per-route fallback chain: primary_model -> variant_1 -> lightweight-fallback. Add button to define policy and a testing harness in Console to simulate failover. Backend already supports routing by policy, mostly UI+config glue needed.
   - Rough effort: 1 backend + 1 frontend sprint.

6) "Simpler eval hooks for quality regression alerts" — Teams running automated evals need an easier way to bind prompt sets to live rollout metrics and get actionable regression alerts.
   - Frequency: medium (platform teams)
   - Impact: medium (prevents regressions during model upgrades)
   - Implementation hunch: add an eval-binding config in Rollouts: link prompt-set ID -> route, with threshold and alerting channel. Leverage existing metrics pipeline to compute regression deltas.
   - Rough effort: 2 sprints (product + metrics plumbing).

Quick impact-effort matrix (verbal):
- Fast wins (low effort, high impact): 1 (latency badge), 3 (prefix SDK), 5 (fallback UI).
- Mid efforts: 2 (Dedicated sizing wizard), 6 (eval hooks).
- Bigger but high value: 4 (cost-sim) — requires careful modeling and data hygiene.

Risk notes and open questions (short list):
- Metrics fidelity: per-route p99 depends on how many synthetic/default routes customers create; need guardrails to avoid noisy signals.
- Data residency / encryption for persisted KV blobs (ask privacy/compliance team).
- Sales expectations: sizing wizard could be treated as a binding quote by procurement — involve pricing/legal.
- Regression detection: threshold tuning will produce noise if too sensitive. Need a beta with a few customers.

Suggested next steps (who does what):
- CS (Ayesha) to run a 2-week micro-pilot for latency badge with 3 customers (analytics product, payments platform, startup B). Capture reactive support ticket change. (owner: Ayesha, due: 2026-08-31)
- Product (Miguel) to scope Dedicated Sizing Wizard spike and map required perf-profile fields; produce a spec doc with API surface. (owner: Miguel, due: 2026-09-10)
- SDK (Riley) to sketch prefix persist API and implement PoC in Node + Python SDKs; test with two customers. (owner: Riley, due: 2026-09-07)
- Security/compliance: quick review of persisted-KV encryption requirements (owner: Samira, due: 2026-08-25)

Notes for research/metrics:
- Pull per-route p95/p99 histograms for last 90 days for customers in pilot bucket.
- Run offline cost-sim for three workload archetypes: chat-streaming short-turn (avg 40 tokens), doc-summarization (avg 600 tokens), embedding-batch (avg 512 tokens).

Appendix: raw snippets (selected customer quotes)
- "We get these weird tail-outs at 750ms and the UI just drops the response. It feels like roulette." — Front-end eng, analytics startup.
- "If we sign a Dedicated commit we can’t easily validate we won’t overpay — a wizard that tells us likely spend would help close the deal." — Procurement lead, mid-market SaaS.
- "We built ad-hoc KV persistence to deal with chat cold starts; it’s brittle and leaks memory across restarts." — CTO, AI-native startup.

Slack seeds / cross refs:
- #cs-product-feedback thread (Aug 5–Aug 10): linked a few support threads and customer quotes.
- Jira: CS-1428 (pilot candidate for latency badge), CS-1439 (prefix-persist PoC).

End of quickscan. This doc is intentionally terse; happy to expand any section into a full spec. If you want a single-sheet spec for the latency badge, I can draft one with required metrics and UI mocks.

-- Ayesha
